_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Reading new SEC Form D filings...

description: Use this when the user wants companies that recently raised money or have long-open roles, such as "which software companies in Texas filed a Form D this month?" or "find companies with a bookkeeper role open 60+ days". Pass the industry, and optionally the region, the role the user's service replaces, lookback_days (1 to 60, default 14) and limit (1 to 15, default 10). Example: {"industry": "software_it", "region": "California"}. Returns companies ranked by score, each with a one-line why and dated signals linking to the SEC filing or job posting. Covers only companies that file a US SEC Form D, based in a US state or in the UK, Canada, Israel, Ireland, Singapore, Australia or Hong Kong. Funds are left out. Roles are checked only when a role is given, on the public job boards of the companies found. A Form D shows funding, not intent to buy. Not for people, contact details or a lookup of one named company, and not for public posts (use find_buying_intent).

industry.description: The buyer's industry. Example call: {"industry": "software_it", "region": "California"}. software_it covers software, SaaS, IT and AI; business_services covers agencies, consultancies and staffing

lookback_days.description: How many days back to look for filings (default 14)

region.description: Where the company is based, such as "California" or "TX". Accepts any US state (name or two-letter code), "US", United Kingdom, Canada, Israel, Ireland, Singapore, Australia, Hong Kong, in any case. Anything else returns unknown_region with the list. Leave out to search everywhere

role.description: The job your service replaces or supports, such as "bookkeeper" or "customer support". When given, the public Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby boards of the companies found are checked for matching roles open 60 or more days

name: find_buyer_signals

companies_checked.description: Newest filings whose offering document was read, at most 12. Say this number in the answer

filings_found.description: Form D filings the SEC search matched in the window, before funds were left out

company.description: Company name as filed with the SEC

location.description: City and state or country from the filing

rank.description: Position by score, 1 is the strongest

score.description: 50 to 115, higher is a stronger signal: 50 for the filing, up to 20 for a fresh filing, up to 15 for a large raise, 5 for a company 2 years old or less, up to 25 for long-open roles

signals.description: The form_d filing first, then any open roles

date.description: Day the filing was made or the role was first published (YYYY-MM-DD)

detail.description: One line on the signal: the raise and amount sold for a form_d, or the job title, days open and location for an open_role

type.description: form_d: an SEC Form D filing. open_role: a matching job posting open 60 or more days

url.description: Link to the SEC filing or the job posting. Give it with the company

why.description: One line on why the company is listed: the filing date, the offering size and any open roles

message.description: Present when status is not ok: what happened and the next step, such as a longer lookback_days or a wider region

notice.description: What a Form D does and does not show. Pass it on

open_roles.description: What the job-board check covered. role is null when no role was given and no board was read

boards_found.description: Public boards found for those companies

companies_checked.description: Companies whose boards were read, at most 6

min_days.description: Days a role must have been open to count

region.description: The region searched, by its full name, or null for everywhere

status.description: ok: leads found. no_data: no operating company matched; message says what to widen. unavailable: SEC EDGAR could not be read; retry in a few minutes

title: Find companies with buyer signals
